claim: For every nonempty finite set E of distinct integers at least 3 with gcd(E)=1 and sigma(E)=sum_{d in E}1/(d-1)>=1/2, every integer k>=1 and every finite set F of labelled occurrences (d,j) with d in E and j>=k, there exist disjoint finite subsets P and Q of the remaining labels such that sum_{(d,j) in Q}d^j-sum_{(d,j) in P}d^j=1; each labelled pair is used at most once, and coincident numerical values from different pairs remain separately available.

quadruple.statement: For every nonempty finite set E of distinct integers at least 3 with gcd(E)=1 and sigma(E)=sum_{d in E}1/(d-1)>=1/2, every integer k>=1 and every finite set F of labelled occurrences (d,j) with d in E and j>=k, there exist disjoint finite subsets P and Q of the remaining labels such that sum_{(d,j) in Q}d^j-sum_{(d,j) in P}d^j=1; each labelled pair is used at most once, and coincident numerical values from different pairs remain separately available.
quadruple.stage: Finite signed subsets of labelled integer pure powers beyond arbitrary positive cutoffs, with exact integer arithmetic and no label reuse.

shape.objects: Every E is a finite rigid set of distinct integer bases; k and finite F vary without bound. Witnesses are finite disjoint subsets of pairs of natural numbers, expressible with Finset, products, integer powers, gcd and sums in Lean/Mathlib. Compatible partial signed supports have common extensions by union on disjoint labels; a gain-producing normalization from an arbitrary seed is not yet known. Finite supports may be random variables, but no spread condition is recorded.
shape.quantifiers: For every such finite E, every positive cutoff k and every finite labelled deletion F, there exist finite disjoint remaining occurrence sets P and Q with exact integer difference one. The leading quantifiers are universal over finite or countable arithmetic objects, and the conclusion has finite existential witnesses. There is no universal quantification over all real sets.
shape.target_quantity: A yes/no existence property: exact signed difference one at a fixed reciprocal-mass assumption of one half, not an optimal numerical bound or density upper bound. An unspecified finite support size depending on E,k,F suffices.
shape.symmetries: The stage combines integer arithmetic and order. Relabelling preserves values and disjoint unions of compatible signed supports preserve coefficient bounds; arbitrary addition of overlapping supports does not. Per-base power shifts preserve that base's label stream but not a common integer multiplier across all bases. Base addition, lowering k or deleting fewer labels preserves represented differences if the hypotheses still hold. No invariant density-increment piece system is supplied.
shape.configuration: Exact relation sum(Q)-sum(P)=1 on disjoint finite allowed labels, every label coefficient in {-1,0,1}; numerical coincidences retain separate labels. The operation must preserve exact value, cutoff, finite deletions and label capacity. Restricting supports or cutting away low exponents can destroy the unit relation, and arbitrary combinations may require a coefficient of magnitude two.
shape.extremal_candidate: No extremal family or optimal constant is asserted; the objective is an exact legal signed unit. Special common-radix constructions are known, but no arbitrary-base motif has been constructed.
shape.finite_certificates: For a fixed E,k,F, a finite signed unit support is a hand-checkable positive certificate, and one is the smallest positive signed difference. Finite bounded coefficient identities are computable small instances in principle; no mathematical process, finite exhaustive reduction or uniform exponent bound is admitted. Absence of a unit in a finite prefix is not a negative certificate.
shape.monotonicity: Yes: enlarging E, lowering k and deleting fewer labels enlarge available signed differences under retained input assumptions. The smallest positive cutoff is one, but all positive cutoffs are required. Increasing the reciprocal threshold weakens the all-E assertion.
shape.uniformity_parameter: The finite base set E, its sizes and values, positive cutoff k and finite deletion F are unbounded. Witness size and maximal exponent may depend on all inputs; no uniform support bound is required.
shape.proof_shape: Move1 assumes a counterexample for analysis, not as a verdict. The persistent signed-tail intersection H is a subgroup and, using full modular subset coverage from collective gcd one, is either zero or Z. A failed unit forces its least positive tail value delta(K) to diverge. Signed tails have a K-dependent bounded gap. An aligned common-radix subset of reciprocal mass at least one half supplies a full signed lattice and, with modular correction on other bases, legal units after all cutoffs. Thus such subsets are excluded from any counterexample. This is a necessary-condition reduction and special-case construction, not a proof of the arbitrary-base claim. The noncommensurate case and the separately stated core and reserve bridge remain open.
shape.neighbours: Known true: classical signed-weight prefix interval criteria, and the common-radix unit constructions inside the accepted ternary and binary proofs. Accepted high-mass positive completeness implies unit differences by taking consecutive represented values and cancelling common labels. The all-E half-mass tail-unit assertion and its special cases outside these configurations remain open. A generic positive central-seed inference even with signed units is known false by acceptance-000004. Bounded signed identities and stronger finite-support candidates have computable small instances. Zero-cutoff signed intervals are comparison results, but do not carry the exact arbitrary-cutoff statement verbatim into a simpler ambient. No reflecting category correspondence, axiom-independence result or countable/uncountable split is recorded.
shape.known_bounds: Accepted high-mass positive completeness at sigma>=3+min{1/4,2/min E} excludes unit counterexamples there. Move1 adds author-verified necessary conditions pending independent review: a counterexample contains no common-radix subset R={B^a} of mass at least one half, in particular no base3, and its power-of-two subfamily has mass below one half. The proof aligns all R exponents at a common multiple and uses the signed-prefix inequality B^r<=2W_r+1. For example it applies to4,8,32 with mass331/651, beyond the earlier4,8,16 alphabet. H is either zero or Z, and failure means delta(K) tends to infinity despite each fixed tail having bounded gaps. A shifted-power example shows the abstract gcd, modular and fixed-tail gap conditions alone are insufficient; it is not a pure-power counterexample. No uniform support bound, finite reduction or general method barrier is proved.
shape.missing_input: Exclude delta(K) tending to infinity for admissible noncommensurate base sets without a common-radix half-mass subfamily, or produce a genuine counterexample. The aligned operation is proved only under that additional structural hypothesis. A separate exact-claim branch can develop its positive reserve consequence. No universal gain-producing ambient operation or recognized external equivalent conjecture is supplied.
shape.base_theory: Classical mathematics in ZFC, using integer arithmetic, finite sets and induction. No extra axiom, forcing or guessing principle is used or known to decide this claim; no uncountable-cardinal difficulty is posed. A correct arithmetic or Lean verification would stay within the base theory, but no mathematical program is admitted.
